key_findings: Flare's 1-year update reports 130M FXRP deployed in DeFi, 7.8M transactions and 21M FXRP on other chains; independent FlareForge snapshot reconciles approximately 144.079M XRP backing 143.995M FXRP and 20.098M remote FXRP.

The underlying XRP/FXRP backing ratio is approximately 100.058%; this is distinct from agent-pool overcollateralization. About 140M of 142.614M XRP in the core vault is escrowed, leaving approximately 2.614M liquid at the snapshot.

Firelight holds approximately 51.9M FXRP, 36.04% of supply, in a slashable cover pool shared across Sentora USD/RWA strategies and a Kraken USDC strategy. It is risk capital, not native XRP staking or insurance.

The live Ethereum Morpho market pairs RLUSD debt with FXRP collateral: approximately $8.44M debt, 90.27% utilization, 99.04% supply from Sentora RLUSD Main, top-three borrower share 90.96%, LLTV 77%, and zero reported bad debt at capture.

Sentora is a strategic ecosystem investment of both Ripple and Flare; its CEO Anthony DeMartino is a former Coinbase Head of Risk. These are investor and personnel links, not evidence of common control.
The Morpho market provides a live RLUSD/FXRP collateral pathway, but FXRP is a representation of existing XRP; the market does not prove new XRP spot purchases or net XRP demand.

Firelight's shared cover can expose FXRP stakers to losses in non-XRP strategies, including USDC and RWA vaults; a secondary source identifies approximately $1M USDT0 in the first-loss buffer on 2026-10-14, but the current official balance and asset composition remain unknown.
Coinbase's XRP cross-collateral product and CFTC 26-17 no-action route remain distinct from the RLUSD listing; the latter's Global Exchange collateral support was announced as future, not yet live.

Circle's Arc mainnet is a major USDC-first institutional and agentic-payment rail: USDC is gas; SBI Group is a founding validator; Coinbase and Binance are exchange participants; Morpho and Aave are credit integrations. Circle claims USDC is 98.8% of agent-driven transaction volume, but gives no absolute denominator.

Flare reports 130M FXRP deployed in DeFi, but explicitly states that only specific events (minting, destination-tag fees, FDC attestations and redemptions) generate Flare fees; not every FXRP trade or loan does. The reported $44,632 cumulative value in FIRE accrues to Flare's fee/burn mechanism, not XRP.

Flare's own one-year article describes the direct XRPL-wallet-to-RLUSD borrow path as the next step; the current live Morpho market uses FXRP collateral on Ethereum. Native XRP collateral borrowing with RLUSD delivered back to XRPL is therefore roadmap, not live.
The Firelight USD Protected vault's exact stablecoin composition is not specified in the official announcement; do not label it RLUSD without contract-level evidence.

competing_hypotheses.claim: FXRP DeFi deployment and collateral use can increase XRP retention and utility.
competing_hypotheses.counter: FXRP is minted against pre-existing XRP; deployment is not net new spot demand, and liquidations/redemptions can reverse flows.

competing_hypotheses.claim: RLUSD borrowing against FXRP creates a new XRP-linked credit market.
competing_hypotheses.counter: The market is small relative to XRP capitalization, highly concentrated on both supply and borrow sides, and permissionless; no evidence of direct Ripple lending.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Firelight cover staking can reduce immediately available FXRP and indirectly lock XRP backing.
competing_hypotheses.counter: Staked FXRP is slashable, exits are delayed, and claims in non-XRP strategies can reduce staker capital.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase collateral eligibility broadens XRP's institutional utility.
competing_hypotheses.counter: Non-US product eligibility is not evidence of actual collateral balances; CFTC 26-17 is conditional no-action relief and not asset-specific use proof.

competing_hypotheses.claim: USDC and RLUSD on XRPL and Coinbase can expand settlement liquidity.
competing_hypotheses.counter: Stablecoin transfers can settle without XRP; stablecoin volume is not automatically XRP demand.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Circle Arc's USDC gas model, SBI validator and Coinbase/Binance participation could capture a large share of institutional and agentic payments, competing with XRPL/Flare for stablecoin settlement.
competing_hypotheses.counter: Circle's 98.8% figure is company-reported without absolute volume or global denominator; Arc is early and uses a permissioned validator set; XRP can remain a bridge/collateral asset even if USDC is the payment/gas asset.

competing_hypotheses.claim: FXRP DeFi growth can increase XRP utility and collateral use.
competing_hypotheses.counter: Flare explicitly routes only specific protocol fees to FLR/FIRE; most FXRP trading/lending does not automatically generate XRP fees or net spot demand.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase is positioning as a multi-issuer stablecoin distribution and collateral platform, not exclusively a Circle/USDC venue.
competing_hypotheses.counter: Coinbase reported an all-time high average USDC balance in Q3; RLUSD Global Exchange collateral support was future at announcement and actual use is unverified.

architecture_decisions.decision: Represent XRP, FXRP, stXRP, RLUSD, USDC and USDt0 as distinct assets with explicit bridge, issuer, backing and receipt relationships.
Admit DeFi collateral features only from timestamped market snapshots with market ID, oracle configuration, borrower/supplier concentration and liquidation history.
Separate native XRP backing ratio from agent collateral ratios and from protocol-level collateralization ratios; never collapse them into one 'collateral ratio'.
Treat cumulative sentiment profile as historical descriptive metadata, not a current feature; require time-windowed, deduplicated, source-independent sentiment observations.
Do not count FXRP minting, bridge volume, Morpho debt or repeated DeFi transactions as net XRP purchases without wallet-level source/sink reconciliation.
Model Circle Arc, XRPL, Flare and Ethereum as distinct settlement/credit rails; record gas asset, validator model, stablecoin, bridge, and institutional participants separately.
Separate XRP utility from token value capture: record FLR/FIRE fees and burns separately from XRP fees, demand and net purchases.
Treat Circle's 98.8% agent-volume statement as a first-party claim without absolute denominator; never compare it directly with XRPL x402 counts or gross transfer volume.
